stories.headline: Dharma Productions locks Rs 250 crore deal to distribute Ramayana across India
stories.what: Karan Johar's Dharma Productions has signed a Rs 250 crore deal to handle the India distribution of the upcoming big-budget film Ramayana. The agreement marks one of the largest distribution deals in recent Bollywood history, signalling the colossal scale of ambition behind the mythological epic. The move consolidates Dharma's position as a dominant force in Indian cinema's distribution landscape.
stories.lens: A Rs 250 crore distribution deal for a single film underscores the high-stakes gamble Bollywood is making on large-scale mythological blockbusters — and how much money is riding on Ramayana's box-office performance.
stories.article:
Dharma Productions, the production house founded by Karan Johar, has secured a Rs 250 crore deal to distribute the upcoming film Ramayana across India, marking one of the most significant distribution agreements the Hindi film industry has seen in recent years. The deal signals the sheer commercial weight being placed behind the mythological epic, which has long been anticipated as a major event film.

The scale of the distribution commitment — Rs 250 crore — reflects industry confidence that Ramayana will draw massive footfalls, but it also places enormous pressure on the film to recover costs at the box office. Distribution deals of this magnitude are typically reserved for films expected to cross blockbuster thresholds, and this one effectively sets a very high bar before a single ticket is sold.

For Dharma Productions, the deal represents a strategic pivot into big-tent event cinema at a time when the studio has been seeking to diversify beyond its traditional romantic-drama fare. Locking in distribution rights at this scale also gives Dharma significant leverage over how and where the film rolls out across the country.

The Ramayana film has been one of Indian cinema's most talked-about projects, with the source material carrying enormous cultural and religious resonance for audiences across the subcontinent. Whether Dharma's Rs 250 crore bet pays off will depend heavily on execution, casting reception and the competitive release landscape when the film eventually arrives.
key_facts: Dharma Productions signs Rs 250 crore India distribution deal for Ramayana
Deal is among the largest distribution agreements in recent Bollywood history
Karan Johar's Dharma Productions is the distributor

stories.headline: Prithvi Shaw's fiancée dismisses break-up rumours after 'cheated on many times' post
stories.what: Prithvi Shaw's fiancée has moved to dismiss circulating break-up rumours after a social media post about being 'cheated on many times' set off speculation about the couple's relationship. The clarification came amid intense public scrutiny of the cricketer's personal life at a time when he is already under the spotlight for his on-field performances. The episode highlights the speed with which celebrity social media posts can spiral into viral controversy.
stories.lens: The episode underscores how quickly a single social media post can engulf a public figure in personal controversy — and how much of India's celebrity culture now plays out, and gets managed, entirely on social platforms.
stories.article:
A social media post apparently referring to being 'cheated on many times' triggered a wave of speculation that cricketer Prithvi Shaw and his fiancée had parted ways. The post spread rapidly across platforms, with fans and gossip accounts quickly connecting it to the couple's relationship.

Shaw's fiancée subsequently moved to put the rumours to rest, publicly dismissing suggestions that the two had broken up. Her clarification drew attention in its own right, given the speed and force with which the original post had generated headlines and social media chatter.

For Prithvi Shaw, the episode adds another dimension of public scrutiny to what has already been a turbulent period in his career. The young cricketer has faced significant attention both for his performances and his personal life, and the latest episode demonstrates how inseparable the two have become in the age of social media celebrity.

The incident is a reminder of the peculiar pressures faced by young Indian public figures who live large portions of their lives online — where ambiguously worded posts become news events and require active management to correct the record.
key_facts: A 'cheated on many times' social media post sparked break-up rumours about Prithvi Shaw
Shaw's fiancée publicly dismissed the break-up speculation
No confirmation of any relationship breakdown was provided

stories.lens: South Indian OTT releases now arrive at a pace that rivals theatrical slates, making the weekly digital lineup essential viewing guidance for millions of regional-language audiences across India.

For viewers, the weekly OTT drop has become a reliable source of fresh content across genres — from drama and comedy to thriller and musical. The titles landing this week span enough variety to keep most tastes covered, whether audiences are looking for grounded family stories, lighthearted entertainment, or something more experimental.

stories.headline: ZEE5 pulls 'Satluj' after government cites security concerns; SGPC and SAD condemn takedown
stories.what: Streaming platform ZEE5 has removed the film 'Satluj' — based on the story of Diljit Dosanjh's 'Punjab 95' — following government intervention citing national security concerns and IT Rules. The Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) have sharply criticised the decision, calling it an attack on creative freedom and the Sikh community's right to tell its own stories. The film had been one of the most anticipated OTT releases, given the controversy that had dogged it since its CBFC delays.
stories.lens: The government-ordered removal of 'Satluj' from ZEE5 raises urgent questions about the reach of unofficial censorship on Indian streaming platforms — and whether OTT is truly a free space for bold, politically sensitive content.
stories.article:
ZEE5 has taken down the film 'Satluj' — previously known as 'Punjab 95' and starring Diljit Dosanjh — after the government cited national security concerns and invoked IT Rules to compel the removal. The abrupt takedown, coming shortly after the film's surprise OTT debut, has sparked a fierce backlash from Sikh religious and political bodies.

The Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) have both condemned the move, accusing the government of suppressing a film that deals with a sensitive chapter of Sikh history. The film, which chronicles events surrounding human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra, had already faced a prolonged battle with the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) before reaching audiences via the streaming route.

The controversy exposes what critics describe as a growing pattern of informal, pressure-based censorship on Indian OTT platforms — a phenomenon that operates outside the formal certification process but achieves the same silencing effect. Unlike theatrical releases, which must clear the CBFC, streaming content in India operates under a self-regulatory framework; however, the government's invocation of IT Rules suggests that framework can be overridden when authorities deem content a security risk.

The removal has reignited a broader debate about artistic freedom, the limits of state intervention in cultural expression, and whether platforms like ZEE5 — which answered to government pressure without a court order — are willing custodians of controversial but legitimate storytelling. For Diljit Dosanjh and the filmmakers, the episode marks another setback in a years-long effort to bring the story of Jaswant Singh Khalra to a wide audience.
key_facts: ZEE5 removed 'Satluj' (Punjab 95) citing government security concerns and IT Rules
SGPC and SAD have condemned the film's removal
CBFC had previously held up the film's theatrical certification
Film is based on human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra's story
